### Praying Powerful Prayers (Acts 4:31)
Author: Kia Stephens
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/your-daily-bible-verse/your-daily-bible-verse-july-13.html
Passage: Acts 4:31
Points:
- Prayer lives often grow routine and dull when believers rely solely on their own strength.
- The early church responded to persecution and threats by gathering to pray with united faith.
- Rather than shrinking back in fear, they asked God for great boldness to speak His word.
- God confirmed His presence and power by shaking the room and filling them with the Holy Spirit.
- Kingdom-focused prayer shifts our perspective from personal troubles to God's worldwide mission.

### Acts 4 Teaches Us How to Pray in Opposition
Author: Kees van Kralingen
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/pray-opposition/
Passage: Acts 4:23-31
Points:
- When facing hostility or intimidation, a believer's first instinct should be prayer.
- Apostolic prayer begins with worship, recognizing God as the sovereign Creator who speaks through Scripture.
- Earthly conspiracies against Jesus did not derail God's predetermined plan of redemption.
- The believers left the opposition to God and asked for boldness to continue preaching.
- The Holy Spirit empowers ordinary Christians to proclaim the gospel courageously in all circumstances.
